title: The leak scan flags a table row whose identifier cell is lower-camel or holds digits (deviceManagementConfigurationPolicy, Win32LobAppAssignmentSettings), because the exemption covers only three capitalised words
goal: kbcommon.leak_hits does not flag a same-line table row with an armor label, a Name: value cell and a lower-camel or digit-bearing identifier cell of 20 or more characters that holds no key material, and still flags a multi-line EC key block and a table row whose identifier cell holds key material

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import kbcommon;L="-"*5+"BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY"+"-"*5;bad=[i for i in ("deviceManagementConfigurationPolicy","windowsAutopilotDeploymentProfile","Win32LobAppAssignmentSettings") if any(k=="secret" for k,_ in kbcommon.leak_hits("| "+L+" | Note: PEM label | "+i+" |"))];print("rows flagged:",bad);sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbcommon as k;L='-'*5+'BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY'+'-'*5;E='-'*5+'END EC PRIVATE KEY'+'-'*5;t=[L+chr(10)+'MHcCAQEEIA7r/Gk3lq9x2Zp0aB1cD2eF3gH4iJ5kL6mN7oP8qR9sT0uV1wX2yZ3a'+chr(10)+E,'| '+L+' | Note: PEM label | MHcCAQEEIA7r/Gk3lq9x2Zp0aB1c |'];r=[bool([h for h in k.leak_hits(x) if h[0]=='secret']) for x in t];print(r);sys.exit(0 if all(r) else 1)

still flags a multi-line EC key block and a table row whose identifier cell holds key material

gates.question: How does the EC/PGP armor lookahead tell a lower-camel or digit-bearing identifier cell from random base64?
options: A whole run of three or more humps, each of three lower-case letters or digits or more, ending at a non-base64 character, is an identifier
Any run with no slash and no upper-case run of two letters is an identifier
gates.recommendation: A whole run of three or more humps, each of three lower-case letters or digits or more, ending at a non-base64 character, is an identifier
gates.answer: A whole run of three or more humps, each of three lower-case letters or digits or more, ending at a non-base64 character, is an identifier
